citation: Reinke, W. M., Herman, K. C., & Dong, N. (2018). The Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management Program: Outcomes from a group randomized trial. Prevention Science, 19(8), 1043-1054. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11121-018-0932-3
report_number: DOI 10.1007/s11121-018-0932-3; ERIC Grantee Submission ED593906. IES award R305A100342 (CFDA 84.324A), U.S. Department of Education, Institute of Education Sciences (5-year grant to Reinke & Herman, University of Missouri).
design: Group (cluster) randomized controlled trial; blocked cluster random assignment at the classroom/teacher level (unit of randomization = Teacher/Class). 9 urban Midwestern-US elementary schools (all implementing SW-PBIS with high fidelity), grades K-3. Randomized across 3 cohorts: 105 teachers (53 IY TCM intervention / 52 wait-list business-as-usual control) and 1817 students at randomization. Comparison = business-as-usual (control teachers placed on a wait list, offered IY TCM 2 years later; no alternative treatment). Outcomes analyzed with 3-level HLM (students nested in teachers nested in schools), 5-imputation MCMC multiple imputation, controlling for pretest + demographics. Final academic-achievement analytic sample = 105 teachers / 1685 students (social/behavioral sample 105 teachers / 1680 students).
problems: (1) SOURCE: legal open-access. Primary text used is the ERIC Grantee Submission (ED593906, https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED593906.pdf) -- a U.S. IES-funded grantee deposit, identical in content/pagination to the published Prevention Science article (the published page numbers 1043-1054 are printed on the grantee PDF). OpenAlex and Unpaywall both report the journal article as closed (no OA), but ERIC hosts the legal grantee version. The standardizing SDs were taken from the article's online supplementary file ESM 1 (Springer 'static-content.springer.com' publisher-served asset 11121_2018_932_MOESM1_ESM.docx -- the publisher's own openly served supplementary material, not a piracy/ResearchGate copy). No Sci-Hub/LibGen/ResearchGate used. (2) STANDARDIZING SD: The paper reports the WJ-III intervention effect only as a raw HLM coefficient b on the WJ-III standard-score scale (Table 3, p.1051); it does NOT print a d-scale effect size or SD for the achievement outcomes in the main text. ESM 1 Supplemental Content Table 2 (baseline descriptives) gives WJ-III Reading control M=98.29/SD=13.06, treatment M=96.46/SD=13.20 (pooled SD=13.13) and WJ-III Math control M=95.14/SD=14.92, treatment M=94.01/SD=14.78 (pooled SD=14.85). I standardized b by these baseline pooled SDs. This is the SD the authors themselves used: their reported baseline effect sizes (Reading -0.14, Math -0.08 in ESM 1) reproduce exactly from these pooled SDs ((96.46-98.29)/13.13=-0.139; (94.01-95.14)/14.85=-0.076). No posttest SD is reported anywhere accessible; WJ-III scores are age-normed standard scores (population SD~15), so the posttest SD is essentially the same as the baseline SD -- using the baseline pooled SD is the defensible, paper-consistent choice (NOT a guess). (3) g VALIDATION: SE(d)=SE(b)/SD reproduces the paper's reported p-values: Reading z=d/se_d=-0.65 -> two-tailed p~.51 (reported p=.53); Math z=-0.08 -> p~.94 (reported p=.94 exact), confirming the b and SE were read correctly from Table 3 and the scaling is internally consistent. (4) PER-ARM n: the academic analytic sample is reported only as a total (105 teachers / 1685 students, p.1048); the per-arm (treatment vs control) student split for the academic sample is not printed (the flowchart's T=833/C=847 = 1680 is the social/behavioral analytic sample). n_t/n_c left null; the cluster-adjusted 3-level HLM SE already accounts for the design, so no central n-based variance recomputation is needed. (5) ICC: the paper reports academic-outcome unconditional ICCs as a RANGE -- 0.03-0.07 at school level and 0.04-0.08 at class level (p.1049) -- not a single per-outcome value, so I recorded the class-level midpoint (0.06) and note the range; cluster_adjusted=true so this ICC is informational only. (6) NON-ACHIEVEMENT outcomes NOT extracted (per spec): all TOCA-C teacher-rated behavior outcomes (concentration problems b=-0.07 ns; disruptive behavior b=-0.04 ns; prosocial behavior b=0.14, p=.038, d=0.13; emotional dysregulation b=-0.15, p<.01, d=-0.14; Table 2) and the T-COMP social competence rating (b=0.14, p=.032, d=0.13, Table 2) are social/emotional/behavior measures, not academic achievement. (7) TEACHER-RATED ACADEMIC COMPETENCE NOT extracted as an achievement contrast: the T-COMP 'academic competence' subscale (Table 3, intervention b=0.11, SE=0.06, p=.074, d=0.08) is a teacher's PERCEPTION/rating of the child's academic competence on a 0-5 Likert scale, not a direct/standardized achievement test -- noted here but excluded; only the two independently administered, standardized WJ-III achievement tests are extracted as achievement effect sizes. (8) Both extracted outcomes are standardized & independent: WJ-III ACH was administered one-on-one by trained research assistants blind to treatment status, so test_type=standardized_independent and both rows are include-eligible under central logic. (9) Both achievement effects are essentially zero / non-significant (g~-0.011 Reading, g~-0.002 Math), consistent with the paper's statement 'There were no main effects on standardized reading or math scores' (p.1049). An academic-achievement outcome DOES exist (flag not raised).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management (IY TCM) -- single TPD treatment arm vs wait-list business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock-Johnson III Normative Update Tests of Achievement (WJ III ACH) -- Broad Reading cluster (standard scores)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of school year, late April/May of the intervention year; pre = early October)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = b/SD where b=-0.15 is the IY TCM 'Intervention' HLM coefficient on WJ-III Broad Reading (Table 3, p.1051), from a 3-level HLM (students in teachers in schools) controlling for WJ-III Reading pretest + demographics. SD = pooled baseline SD of WJ-III Reading standard scores = sqrt((13.06^2+13.20^2)/2) = 13.13 (ESM 1 Supplemental Content Table 2; same SD the authors used to report baseline ES -0.14). d = -0.15/13.13 = -0.01142. se_d = SE(b)/SD = 0.23/13.13 = 0.01752. J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.99955 (df = 1685-2 = 1683). g = J*d = -0.01142; g_se = J*se_d = 0.01751; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.000307. P-value check: z = d/se_d = -0.652 -> two-tailed p~.51 vs reported p=.53.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3 (HLM results for academic outcomes), p.1051; measure description p.1047-1048; analytic sample p.1048; ICC p.1049; SDs from ESM 1 Supplemental Content Table 2
effect_sizes.notes: Non-significant near-zero achievement effect: b=-0.15, SE=0.23, p=.53 (Table 3). WJ-III Broad Reading -> Reading. Independently administered by trained RAs blind to condition (p.1048) -> standardized_independent. Academic analytic sample = 105 teachers / 1685 students; per-arm n split not reported (the flowchart's T=833/C=847 is the social/behavioral sample). Pretest-adjusted (WJ-III Reading pretest) and cluster-adjusted (3-level HLM). sd_t/sd_c are BASELINE standard-score SDs (ESM 1); posttest SD not reported but WJ-III SS is age-normed so baseline SD is the appropriate standardizer. ICC=0.06 = midpoint of the reported class-level unconditional ICC range 0.04-0.08 for academic outcomes (school-level range 0.03-0.07); informational only since cluster_adjusted=true.
